clues: a series of short beeps sounds every time the PC is switched on
the screen stays black after the startup beeps
the case fans and the power light come on, but the PC never shows a picture
the PC has beeped at startup since it was carried to a new desk last week

answer.cause: a memory module that has worked loose in its slot
answer.action: Reseat the memory modules firmly until the slot latches lock

firstStep: Look up the beep code in the motherboard manual
appliesWhen: the PC beeps at power-on and stops because a memory module is not fully seated
explanation: POST checks the RAM early, and when it cannot use a module it stops and sounds a beep code instead of showing video. Moving a PC or heating and cooling over time can loosen a module. Look up the pattern in the motherboard documentation, then reseat the module.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the clock shows a date years in the past after each cold start
custom firmware settings are lost whenever the PC is unplugged overnight
after a night unplugged, the PC opens the firmware setup screen instead of loading Windows
the seven-year-old PC now shows a warning about the system time at each startup

answer.cause: a dead CMOS battery
answer.action: Replace the coin cell on the motherboard and enter the firmware settings again

firstStep: Test the coin cell's voltage with a multimeter
appliesWhen: the date, time, and firmware settings reset each time the PC loses wall power
explanation: The small lithium coin cell (often a CR2032) keeps the clock and firmware settings while the PC is unplugged. When it runs down, the date returns to a default and the other settings are lost. Replace it, then set the date, time, and settings again.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: several small cylinders on the motherboard bulge at the top
brown crust has leaked from the top of the bulging parts on the board
the PC restarts on its own several times a day
the random restarts continue after a clean reinstall of Windows

answer.cause: swollen capacitors on the motherboard
answer.action: Replace the motherboard

appliesWhen: parts on the board are visibly bulging or leaking and the PC restarts without warning
explanation: Capacitors that fail swell from gas inside them and can leak electrolyte, which makes the PC restart, shut down, or crash. Replacing single capacitors takes special training, so the usual fix is a new motherboard. Do not touch the residue.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: a sharp burning smell comes from the rear vent next to the AC cord
a thin wisp of smoke rose from the back grille of the PC
the burning smell is strongest at the top rear corner of the case
the burning smell started today on a PC that has run for years without trouble

answer.cause: a power supply that is about to fail
answer.action: Replace the power supply with a new unit

firstStep: Shut the PC down and unplug it at once
appliesWhen: a burning smell or smoke comes from the power supply area of the case
explanation: A burning smell or smoke from the power supply means it is close to failing and could short out or start a fire. Never open a power supply, because its capacitors hold a dangerous charge; replace the whole unit.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: nothing happens when the front power button is pressed
no lights or fans come on at all when the PC is switched on
a desk lamp works in the same wall outlet that the dead PC uses
a new AC cord made no difference to the dead PC
the PC has not powered on since a thunderstorm passed through last night

answer.cause: a dead power supply
answer.action: Replace the power supply with a known good unit

firstStep: Test the unit with a power supply tester
appliesWhen: the PC shows no sign of life even though the outlet and the AC cord are good
explanation: When the outlet and the cord are good but nothing at all lights or spins, the power supply is the most likely failed part, often after a spike. A PSU tester or a known good unit confirms it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC and its monitor both show no lights and will not turn on
a desk lamp plugged in beside the dead PC under the desk is also dark
the PC and monitor have been dead since a cleaner worked under the desk this morning
the wall outlet next to the door works, but nothing under the desk powers on

answer.cause: a power strip that is switched off or tripped
answer.action: Switch on or reset the power strip, or plug the PC into a working outlet

appliesWhen: every device on the same power strip is dead at once
explanation: When the PC, the monitor, and a lamp on the same strip are all dark, the problem is before the PC: the strip was switched off, tripped, or unplugged. Always check the power source before you open the case.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC shuts down after about 30 minutes of work
after each shutdown the PC starts again normally once it has cooled for a while
the PC that keeps shutting down sits on the floor of a dusty loading area
very little air comes out of the rear vents before each shutdown
the firmware shows the processor near its maximum temperature after a few minutes

answer.cause: dust clogging the heat sink and fans
answer.action: Clean the heat sink, fans, and vents with compressed air

firstStep: Check the processor temperature and fan speeds in the firmware setup
appliesWhen: the PC overheats in a dirty place because dust blocks the air flow
explanation: Dust and dirt build up on fans and heat sinks in dirty places such as warehouses, so heat cannot leave the case and the PC shuts down to protect itself. Blow the dust out with compressed air, holding the fans still.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the firmware shows 0 RPM on the processor cooler header
the PC shuts down a few minutes after it starts
the inside of the case is clean, yet the PC shuts down after a few minutes
the early shutdowns began when a loud whine that came from the PC for weeks suddenly stopped

answer.cause: a failed CPU fan
answer.action: Replace the CPU fan with one that fits the heat sink and socket

appliesWhen: the processor cooler has stopped turning, so the PC overheats within minutes
explanation: A fan that has stopped cannot move heat away from the processor, so the PC overheats and shuts down quickly. A noisy bearing often comes before the fan stops. Fit a compatible replacement fan.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC has shut down under load since the processor was upgraded
the processor temperature climbs past 95 °C within minutes
the cooler's fan spins at full speed while the processor overheats
the cooler on the overheating processor moves when it is touched lightly

answer.cause: a heat sink that is not seated firmly on the CPU
answer.action: Clean off the old thermal paste, apply new paste, and fasten the heat sink securely

appliesWhen: the processor overheats right after it was installed because the cooler does not sit flat on it
explanation: Heat moves from the processor to the heat sink only through firm contact and a thin layer of thermal paste. A loose cooler or air gaps in the paste make the CPU overheat fast, even with a working fan. Clean, re-paste, and fasten it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: different applications close without warning
a blue stop screen appears a few times a week
the stop screens show the same memory address each time
the crashes continue although the system drive passes all its health checks
the crashes continued after a clean reinstall of Windows

answer.cause: a faulty memory module
answer.action: Replace the failing memory module

firstStep: Run the Windows Memory Diagnostic tool
appliesWhen: applications crash and stop screens appear because a memory module is failing
explanation: Failing RAM often looks like a software problem: application crashes and proprietary crash screens such as the Windows BSOD. An error at the same memory address each time points to physical memory. A memory test confirms it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the startup screen reports less RAM than was installed
the new modules are on the qualified list, but the PC does not count all the new memory
the new modules work in another PC, but this PC reports less memory than is installed
reseating the new modules did not change the low memory total

answer.cause: firmware that is too old to recognize the new memory
answer.action: Update (flash) the UEFI/BIOS firmware

appliesWhen: compatible new memory is not recognized because the firmware is out of date
explanation: When new, compatible RAM is not counted at POST, the firmware may not have the code to identify it. Flashing the UEFI/BIOS to the latest version adds support for newer parts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC is slow whenever several programs are open
the Task Manager view shows memory use above 90 percent while the PC crawls
the PC that slows down with several programs open has only 4 GB installed
the PC is quick again after a restart until the user opens the usual programs

answer.cause: too little RAM for the user's workload
answer.action: Add more RAM to the PC

appliesWhen: the PC is slow because memory use is near 100 percent with the user's normal programs
explanation: When physical memory runs out, Windows moves data to the paging file on the drive, which is much slower, so the whole PC feels sluggish. More RAM fixes this.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC restarts as soon as a 3D game starts
the restarts began after a high-end graphics card was added last week
the PC was stable before the upgrade, but now it restarts under heavy load
temperatures stay normal before each restart

answer.cause: a power supply too small for the new components
answer.action: Install a power supply with a higher wattage rating

appliesWhen: the PC restarts under load after an upgrade added parts that draw more power
explanation: New parts such as a large graphics card can draw more power than the old supply can give, so the PC restarts under load. When you upgrade components, check whether the power supply needs an upgrade too.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power

clues: a loud ticking or buzzing sound comes from inside the case
the noise began after a technician added a second drive
the noise changes when the side panel is pressed
temperatures are normal despite the noise in the case

answer.cause: a cable touching a fan blade
answer.action: Reroute and tie the cables away from the fans

appliesWhen: a buzzing or ticking noise started after work inside the case left something in the path of a fan
explanation: A wire brushing a CPU or case fan makes a buzzing or ticking noise. Route and tie the cables clear of the fans; this also improves air flow.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: a loud whine comes from the back corner where the AC cord plugs in
the whine gets louder and quieter by turns
little air comes out of the rear vent by the AC cord, which used to blow warm air
the CPU and case fans run quietly while the rear corner whines

answer.cause: a failing fan inside the power supply
answer.action: Replace the whole power supply without opening it

appliesWhen: a loud whine comes from the power supply corner and little air leaves its vent
explanation: A failing power supply fan can whine or change speed, and it soon lets the supply overheat. For the A+ exam, never open the power supply to fix the fan; replace the unit.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the screen has stayed black since a graphics card was installed yesterday
the PC beeps once at startup, yet nothing appears on the screen
the drive light flickers as if Windows is loading, but the screen shows nothing
the monitor shows its no-signal message

answer.cause: a monitor cable plugged into the motherboard's video port
answer.action: Connect the monitor cable to a port on the new graphics card

appliesWhen: a new graphics card is installed but the monitor is still connected to the motherboard's own video port
explanation: Most motherboards turn off their built-in video when an expansion graphics card is installed. The PC boots normally, but a monitor on the motherboard port gets no signal. Move the cable to the graphics card.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: a regular clicking sound comes from the drive
files take a long time to open
the computer froze twice with a loud click
the drive that clicks is five years old

answer.cause: a failing mechanical hard drive
answer.action: Replace the hard drive with a new drive

firstStep: Back up the important data at once
appliesWhen: a mechanical drive clicks in a regular rhythm and starts to lock up
explanation: A regular, rhythmic clicking from a hard drive means it is failing or has failed. Do not wait: copy the data to a good drive and replace the failing one.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: a grinding, scraping noise comes from the drive bay
the noise sounds like fingernails on a chalkboard
the PC stopped responding while the noise was loud
the noise is not from the fans, which were just replaced

answer.cause: read/write heads that have crashed into the disk platters
answer.action: Power off at once, recover what data is possible, and replace the drive

appliesWhen: a mechanical drive makes a grinding or scraping noise because its heads touch the platters
explanation: A grinding or scraping noise from a mechanical drive means the motor has failed or the heads are cutting into the platters. Stop using the drive, get the data off it if you can, and replace it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC tries to start from the network and then reports that no bootable device was found
the system drive is listed in the firmware setup, but Windows does not load on its own
the PC starts Windows only when the drive is chosen from the one-time startup menu
the PC has not loaded Windows on its own since the firmware was updated yesterday

answer.cause: a wrong boot order in the firmware
answer.action: Put the system drive first in the UEFI/BIOS boot sequence

appliesWhen: the drive is detected and works, but the firmware tries other devices first
explanation: The firmware boots from the devices in the order it lists. If the network or another device comes first, the PC can report that no bootable device was found even though the system drive is fine. A firmware update or reset can change the order.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the firmware setup does not list the system drive
the PC has reported that no bootable device was found since it was moved to another office yesterday
the drive spins up and is quiet at startup, but the firmware cannot see it
the missing drive is detected when it is fitted in another PC

answer.cause: a loose or damaged SATA data cable
answer.action: Reseat the data cable at both ends or replace it

appliesWhen: the firmware cannot detect a quiet, working drive because its data connection is loose
explanation: If the firmware does not detect a drive that spins normally, check the connections first. A SATA data cable can work loose when a PC is moved, or it can be damaged. Reseat it or try a new cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the second drive installed in the PC today does not appear in File Explorer
the firmware lists the new drive, but Windows shows no drive letter for it
the new disk that is missing from File Explorer shows only unallocated space in Disk Management
the new drive passes the maker's diagnostic test, but the user cannot save files to it

answer.cause: a new drive that has not been set up with a partition and a volume
answer.action: Initialize the disk in Disk Management, then create and format a volume with a drive letter

appliesWhen: the firmware sees a new drive but Windows has no volume on it
explanation: Windows can use a drive only after it is initialized, partitioned, formatted, and given a drive letter. If the firmware detects the drive but File Explorer does not show it, prepare it in Disk Management.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the system drive has 3 GB free out of 500 GB
saving files takes much longer than it used to
a low disk space warning keeps appearing
saving is slow even though the drive passes a S.M.A.R.T. health check

answer.cause: a system drive that is almost full
answer.action: Free up space with Disk Cleanup or move files to another drive

appliesWhen: the drive is slow because it has almost no free space left
explanation: A drive needs free space (at least 10 percent) for temporary files and the paging file. With almost none left, reads and writes take much longer. Remove files and unused apps or move data to another drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: files on the mechanical drive take a little longer to open every month
the slow mechanical drive still has 40 percent free space
the PC has slowed since the scheduled drive maintenance was turned off two years ago
the drive passes a S.M.A.R.T. health check although files open more slowly each month

answer.cause: a heavily fragmented hard disk drive
answer.action: Analyze and defragment the drive with Optimize Drives

appliesWhen: a mechanical drive slows down over time because its files are stored in scattered pieces
explanation: When file pieces are scattered across a mechanical drive, the heads move more to read them and read/write times grow. Defragmenting puts the data back in order. Do not defragment SSDs often.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the drive activity light stays lit and the PC is sluggish even when the user is idle
the Task Manager view shows an unknown app reading and writing the disk all day
the PC has been sluggish since the user installed a free movie download app last month
the drive has plenty of free space, but its activity light never goes out

answer.cause: file-sharing software that keeps the drive busy
answer.action: Remove the peer-to-peer file-sharing software and scan for malware

appliesWhen: an unwanted app such as a torrent client keeps the drive working all the time
explanation: A drive light that blinks far more than usual shows that the drive is working hard. Torrent and other P2P clients, or malware, can keep a drive busy and slow everything else. Remove them and scan the drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: a S.M.A.R.T. warning appears at startup
wmic diskdrive get status reports Pred Fail
the drive diagnostic tool shows the reallocated sector count rising each week
the drive still works for now, but the warning appears at every startup

answer.cause: a drive that is predicting its own failure
answer.action: Back up the data and replace the drive before it fails

appliesWhen: the drive's own monitoring data warns of a coming failure
explanation: S.M.A.R.T. monitors drive health and can warn before a drive fails; a status other than OK, or a rising count of bad sectors, is a reason to act. Back up now and plan the replacement.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: users wait several seconds each time they save a record
a benchmark shows 40 percent fewer operations per second than the drive's rating
saves have grown slower steadily over six months
the slow drives are SSDs and are less than half full

answer.cause: aging drives whose IOPS are too low for the workload
answer.action: Replace the drives with new, faster SSDs

appliesWhen: a benchmark shows the drives deliver far fewer IOPS than their rating, and the number keeps falling
explanation: IOPS measures how many reads and writes a drive completes each second. Results 10 to 20 percent below the vendor's numbers are normal, but 25 percent or more below, or a steady decline, means the drives need attention or replacement.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the array utility at startup shows the volume as degraded
an amber light is lit on one drive bay
the server still starts and all files open, despite the array warning at startup
the degraded volume was built from two drives that hold the same data

answer.cause: a failed drive in the RAID 1 mirror
answer.action: Replace the failed drive and rebuild the mirror

appliesWhen: one drive of a two-drive mirror has failed while the data stays available
explanation: A RAID 1 mirror keeps a full copy on each drive, so one failure leaves a degraded but working volume. Replace the failed member and rebuild the array before the other drive fails too. RAID is not a backup.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the data volume made of two drives is gone
one of the two drives no longer spins up
the lost volume was set up for speed with no redundancy
the other drive tests good, but the volume cannot be opened

answer.cause: a failed drive in a striped RAID 0 array
answer.action: Replace the drive, create the array again, and restore the data from backup

appliesWhen: one drive of a stripe set has failed, so the whole volume and its data are lost
explanation: RAID 0 spreads data across the drives with no redundancy, so one failed drive destroys the whole volume. Replace the drive, rebuild the array, and restore the data from the backup.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the array disappeared right after a firmware update
the array setup screen no longer opens at startup
the firmware lists each drive as a separate disk instead of the array
the PC reports that no bootable device was found

answer.cause: the SATA mode reset from RAID to AHCI
answer.action: Set the SATA mode back to RAID in the UEFI/BIOS setup

appliesWhen: the drives are fine but the firmware's SATA setting no longer enables the array
explanation: Motherboard RAID works only when the SATA mode is set to RAID. A firmware update or a reset to defaults returns it to AHCI, so the array utility does not load and the array is missing. Change the setting back.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

clues: no drive of the array appears at startup
the add-in card's setup screen no longer appears at startup
the add-in card's status light is dark and the array is missing
each missing drive tests good in another server

answer.cause: a failed RAID controller card
answer.action: Replace the RAID controller card with a compatible model

appliesWhen: all the drives are good but the add-in card that runs the array has failed
explanation: When every drive of an array is missing but each drive works elsewhere, the controller is the shared failure point. Check that the card is seated, then replace it with a compatible controller and import the array.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the NAS beeps loudly every few seconds
one drive bay on the NAS shows a red light
the shared folders still open but more slowly than before
the beeping NAS holds four drives with parity across them

answer.cause: a failed drive in the RAID 5 array
answer.action: Replace the failed drive and let the array rebuild

firstStep: Check the management utility for the alert
appliesWhen: an alarm sounds because one drive of a parity array has failed
explanation: NAS and RAID devices sound alarms and light a bay LED when a drive fails. RAID 5 keeps working with one failed drive, but a second failure loses the array, so replace the drive and rebuild.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: files saved during storms are often corrupt
files saved while the office lights dim at copier startup open corrupted
the drive passes S.M.A.R.T. and surface tests, yet some saved files are corrupt
the PC that saves corrupt files is plugged straight into the wall outlet

answer.cause: power surges and drops that interrupt writes to the drive
answer.action: Connect the PC to a UPS or a surge suppressor

appliesWhen: files are corrupted because unstable power interrupts writes to a healthy drive
explanation: A file written during a surge or drop can be stored corrupt even on a healthy drive. Check that the power supply is big enough and protect the PC with a UPS or power conditioning.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

clues: the monitor shows a no-signal message on a black screen
the monitor's power light is on, but the screen shows no picture
the screen has been blank since the PC was moved from an HDMI cable to a DisplayPort cable today
the PC starts normally and the drive light flickers, but the monitor shows nothing

answer.cause: the monitor set to the wrong input
answer.action: Select the correct input source in the monitor's on-screen menu

appliesWhen: the monitor is on but looks for the signal on a different port
explanation: A monitor with several ports shows a black screen when its on-screen display is set to one port and the PC is connected to another. Choose the matching input in the OSD.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the image flickers when the desk is bumped
the screen goes black for a second and then returns
the plug at the back of the flickering monitor has a bent pin
the flicker stays when a known good monitor is connected

answer.cause: a loose or damaged video cable
answer.action: Reseat the video cable or replace it with a quality cable

appliesWhen: the image cuts out or flickers when the connection is moved
explanation: Poor connections and worn or damaged cables cause flicker, fuzziness, and random blackouts. Check the plugs and the whole cable length, and replace a damaged cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the fan runs but no light comes from the lens
a warning light on the case is lit and nothing appears on the screen
the projector that shows no image has run for thousands of hours
the laptop shows the presentation on its own screen, but nothing is projected

answer.cause: a burnt-out projector lamp
answer.action: Replace the lamp with the approved type for the model and reset the lamp counter

appliesWhen: the projector powers on but gives no light at all
explanation: A projector lamp has a limited life, and when it burns out no light comes from the lens. Let the projector cool and unplug it, fit the exact lamp type, then reset the lamp hour counter in the OSD.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the projected text is blurry everywhere on the screen
the image has been blurry since the projector was moved farther from the screen this morning
the laptop's own screen is sharp while the projected image is soft
the blurry image has a normal rectangle shape

answer.cause: a projector that is out of focus
answer.action: Adjust the focus ring or focus setting on the projector

appliesWhen: a projected image is blurry all over after the projector moved
explanation: A projector must be focused for its distance to the screen. After it is moved, turn the focus ring on the lens or use the focus setting in its menu.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: text looks soft and blurry on the new monitor
circles look stretched into ovals
on the blurry monitor, the Display settings page shows a value that is not marked as recommended
the same PC looked sharp on the old monitor, but text is soft on the new one

answer.cause: a resolution that does not match the monitor's native resolution
answer.action: Set the display to its recommended native resolution

appliesWhen: the image is fuzzy or stretched because the resolution or aspect ratio does not match the panel
explanation: A flat panel looks sharp only at its native resolution. A different resolution or aspect ratio makes the image fuzzy, stretched, or boxed in. Choose the recommended resolution in Display settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: icons and text look huge
dialog boxes do not fit and their buttons are cut off
icons look huge even though the resolution is set to the recommended value
text and icons have looked huge since a visitor changed the display options yesterday

answer.cause: a display scale setting that is set too high
answer.action: Lower the scale percentage in Windows Display settings

appliesWhen: items on screen are oversized although the resolution is correct
explanation: Windows scaling enlarges text and items at the same resolution. Too high a scale makes everything oversized and cuts off windows; set a lower percentage in Display settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: a faint outline of the taskbar stays visible over every image
the ghost outline matches the dashboard that the display showed all day for two years
the ghost image is still there after the screen was off for a day
the panel with the ghost image is an OLED display

answer.cause: permanent burn-in on the panel
answer.action: Replace the display

appliesWhen: a faint copy of an old static image stays on screen whatever is shown
explanation: A static image shown for a long time can wear OLED pixels unevenly and leave a permanent ghost image. Power cycling helps only short-term image retention; real burn-in needs a new display.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: a few tiny black dots stay in the same place on the screen
the dots show up best on a white background
a screen repair utility made no change to the black dots
the dots appear on every picture and in the firmware screen

answer.cause: dead pixels on the LCD panel
answer.action: Replace the monitor or have the panel replaced under warranty

appliesWhen: a few points on the panel never light up
explanation: Dead pixels never light, so they show as black dots on a white screen. Repair utilities and power cycling sometimes free a stuck pixel, but a dead one means replacing the panel.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the screen seems to flicker slightly all the time
the user gets headaches after an hour at the flickering screen
the flicker started after the display settings were reset
the cable and monitor work without flicker on another PC

answer.cause: a refresh rate set too low for the monitor
answer.action: Raise the refresh rate in Advanced display settings

appliesWhen: the screen flickers steadily because the image is redrawn too few times a second
explanation: The refresh rate is how often the image is redrawn each second. Set too low, or to a rate the monitor does not support, it causes flicker or a flashing screen. Set it to a rate the monitor supports.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the image is very dark even with every adjustment at maximum
a flashlight held at the screen shows the image faintly
the screen flickered for weeks before it went dark
the laptop shows a bright image on an external monitor

answer.cause: a failing backlight
answer.action: Replace the backlight or the display panel

appliesWhen: the image is barely visible and no setting makes it bright enough
explanation: A flat panel makes its image bright with a backlight. When the backlight (or its inverter) fails, the image is still there but very dim, and flicker often comes first. Replace the failed part.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the screen became dark after a child played with the keyboard
the image is clear but dark
the screen is equally dark on battery and on AC power
the dark screen has never flickered

answer.cause: a brightness setting that is turned all the way down
answer.action: Raise the brightness with the function keys or the display settings

appliesWhen: the screen is dim only because the brightness control is set low
explanation: A dim image is often only a setting. On a laptop, the function keys change brightness; on a monitor, use the OSD. Set brightness first, then contrast.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: photos look too blue on one monitor only
the two monitors show the same image in different colors
the colors changed after a coworker pressed the buttons on that monitor last week
the blue-tinted monitor's cable shows correct colors on the other monitor

answer.cause: monitor color settings that are out of adjustment
answer.action: Calibrate the monitor or reset it to factory settings in its on-screen menu

appliesWhen: the colors are wrong because the monitor's color, brightness, or contrast settings were changed
explanation: Wrong colors on one display, with a good cable, usually come from its own settings. Reset the monitor in its OSD, or calibrate it with the Windows Display Color Calibration tool (dccw).
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the video plays on the meeting room TV but no sound comes from it
the audio plays quietly from the keyboard area instead of the TV
the TV stays silent although its volume is up and it is not muted
one HDMI cable carries the picture to the TV, but no sound reaches it

answer.cause: a sound output setting that points to the built-in speakers instead of the display
answer.action: Choose the TV as the output device in Sound settings

appliesWhen: the display can play sound but Windows sends the audio to another device
explanation: HDMI and DisplayPort carry audio as well as video, but Windows must use the display as its output device. Pick it in Sound settings and check the volume mixer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the monitor's built-in speakers stay silent
the silent monitor is connected with a wide white plug that has thumbscrews
no sound plays from the monitor although the correct output device is chosen in Sound settings
the monitor's speakers work when it is connected to a game console

answer.cause: a DVI connection, which carries no audio
answer.action: Connect the monitor with an HDMI or DisplayPort cable instead

appliesWhen: the picture works but the cable type cannot carry sound to the display
explanation: DVI carries only video, so speakers in a monitor get no sound over it. HDMI and DisplayPort carry both video and audio.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the projector turns itself off after about 40 minutes
it turns on again after it has cooled down
a temperature warning light flashes just before it goes off
a layer of dust covers the intake grille of the projector that keeps shutting off

answer.cause: a projector overheating because its air filter is clogged
answer.action: Clean or replace the projector's air filter and clear the vents

appliesWhen: the projector shuts down by itself after it has run for a while because hot air cannot leave it
explanation: Projectors make a lot of heat and shut themselves off when they overheat. Clean the air filter, keep the vents clear, give the unit room to exhaust, and check the cooling fan.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the projected image is wider at the top than at the bottom
the misshapen image comes from a projector on a low table aimed up at the screen
the laptop's own screen looks normal while the projected image is out of shape
the text in the misshapen image is sharp in the middle

answer.cause: a projector that is tilted with no keystone correction
answer.action: Adjust the keystone correction on the projector

appliesWhen: a projected image is shaped like a trapezoid because the projector is aimed at an angle
explanation: A projector aimed up or down at the screen makes a trapezoid-shaped image. Keystone correction in the projector's menu squares the image again.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues

clues: the display settings offer only a low resolution after an update
the Device Manager list shows a basic display adapter since the update
games show odd blocks and lines
the monitor that now offers only low resolutions works well on another PC

answer.cause: a corrupt or wrong display driver
answer.action: Roll back or reinstall the correct display driver

appliesWhen: the image is distorted or stuck at a low resolution because the video driver is wrong or damaged
explanation: A failed, wrong, or bad update to the video driver can leave Windows in low-resolution mode or distort the image. Update the driver in Device Manager, or roll it back to the version that worked.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the device lasts only half a morning on a full charge
the battery health page in settings reports only 68 percent
the device that runs out of charge so fast is four years old and is charged every night
the device shuts off at 20 percent while it runs a normal app

answer.cause: a worn battery that has lost most of its capacity
answer.action: Replace the battery, or the device if the battery cannot be replaced

firstStep: Check the battery health page in the device settings
appliesWhen: the device is old and its battery runs down very fast with normal use
explanation: A battery handles only a few hundred charge cycles, so a phone charged daily wears its battery out in three to five years. Low maximum capacity and sudden shutdowns mean the battery must be replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the screen has lifted away from the frame along one edge
the back of the case bulges and the device rocks on a flat desk
the case began to bulge after the device was left on a cheap car charger for weeks
the case seam has cracked open near the bottom

answer.cause: a swollen lithium-ion battery
answer.action: Power the device off, unplug it, and send it for battery replacement or safe recycling

appliesWhen: the case is pushed out of shape because the battery inside has expanded
explanation: Overcharging, age, the wrong charger, or a defect can make the cells swell and push the screen and case apart. A swollen battery can catch fire, so stop using and charging the device and have the battery removed and recycled.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the screen has not worked properly since the device fell face down on a tile floor
a web of cracks spreads out from one corner
tiny glass slivers come off when the user swipes
parts of the picture show black blotches under the cracks

answer.cause: physical impact damage to the display
answer.action: Replace the cracked display assembly or the device

appliesWhen: the device was dropped and the front glass and panel are cracked
explanation: A drop can crack the cover glass and the panel under it, and broken glass can cut the user. The fix is a new display assembly or a new device; screen protectors and drop-resistant cases help prevent it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the device charges only when the cord is held at a certain angle
the charging cord is frayed and bent sharply just behind the plug
one connector end of the charging cord has a brown burn mark
the device charges normally from a coworker's cord but not from its own

answer.cause: a damaged charging cable
answer.action: Replace the charging cable with a good one

firstStep: Inspect the cable for cuts, bends, and burn marks
appliesWhen: the cord is cut, bent, or burned and the device charges only with other cords
explanation: The cable is the first thing to check when a mobile device charges poorly, and it is the most common culprit. Rips, sharp bends, and burn marks mean the cable must be replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the charging plug no longer clicks all the way in
the device that charges only now and then is carried loose in a pocket every day
a flashlight shows gray fluff stuck at the back of the charging opening
several known good cords charge the device only now and then

answer.cause: lint and debris packed in the charging port
answer.action: Clean out the charging port with compressed air and a nonmetal pick

firstStep: Look into the charging port with a flashlight
appliesWhen: the connector opening is packed with lint and the plug cannot seat fully
explanation: Pocket lint builds up in the charging port until the plug cannot make full contact. Clear it with compressed air and a toothpick or cotton swab, with the device turned off.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices

clues: the charging opening is bent out of shape after the device fell on its cord
no cable charges the device or connects it to a computer
the charging opening is clean, but its center tab is cracked
the device charges normally on a wireless pad but not from any cable

answer.cause: a physically damaged charging port
answer.action: Have the port repaired or replace the device

appliesWhen: the connector itself is bent or broken and no cable works in it
explanation: A port that is visibly bent or broken cannot be fixed by cleaning or a new cable. The only remedy is to replace the port, which on many phones means replacing the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: all Wi-Fi, cellular data, and Bluetooth links stopped at the same moment
the device has had no connections since the user got off a flight this morning
the earbuds and the car audio both fail to connect
the signal bars are gone even next to the office access point

answer.cause: airplane mode left turned on
answer.action: Turn off airplane mode in the quick settings

appliesWhen: every radio on the device is off at once because of one setting
explanation: Airplane mode turns off all the radios at once, so Wi-Fi, cellular, and Bluetooth fail together. Check that it is off before you troubleshoot each connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the device keeps dropping the Wi-Fi connection at the far end of the building
the dropped connection is strong again in the room next to the access point
the connection drops at the user's desk, which has two cinder-block walls between it and the access point
other devices at the same desk drop the Wi-Fi too

answer.cause: a weak Wi-Fi signal from distance and walls
answer.action: Move closer to the access point or add an access point near the user

appliesWhen: the device is far from the access point or behind thick walls
explanation: Poor or intermittent connectivity on mobile devices usually comes from distance, and steel or cinder-block walls shorten the range a lot. Moving closer or adding an access point fixes it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the device has not joined the office Wi-Fi since the wireless password changed over the weekend
the device shows the office network but keeps saying it cannot join
cellular data and Bluetooth work normally, but the office Wi-Fi will not connect
a new laptop joins the same network without trouble while the device cannot

answer.cause: a saved Wi-Fi profile with an old passphrase
answer.action: Forget the network and join it again with the new passphrase

appliesWhen: the network's password changed and the device still tries the old one
explanation: A device keeps the passphrase it saved when it first joined a network. After the passphrase changes, forgetting the network and joining it again stores the new one.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the device has acted up since it slipped into a sink full of water
the speaker sounds muffled and the picture flickers
the device that fell in the water has no IP67 or IP68 rating
fog shows under the camera lens

answer.cause: liquid damage inside the device
answer.action: Power it off at once, remove the case and SIM card, and let it dry fully before testing

appliesWhen: the device was dropped in or soaked with a liquid
explanation: Liquid can short the circuits while the device is on. Turn it off, take off the case and remove the cards, dry it, and let it dry for about 48 hours before you power it on.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the device gets too hot to hold during long navigation runs
the device overheats where it sits on the dashboard in direct sunlight inside a thick rubber case
the battery drains fast while the map app runs
the device warns that charging is paused until it cools

answer.cause: heavy app use in a hot spot with poor airflow
answer.action: Close the heavy apps, use a case with better airflow, and keep the device out of direct sunlight

appliesWhen: a demanding app runs for a long time while the device sits in heat or in a case that traps heat
explanation: GPS, games, and streaming apps work the processor and battery hard, and direct sun and a tight case trap the heat. Removing the heat sources and closing the apps lets the device cool; if it still overheats, test the battery.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: taps in the lower third of the display do nothing
the display ignores taps there even though the picture looks perfect and has no cracks
the dead touch area stays after a restart
the stylus also fails in the same area

answer.cause: a failed digitizer
answer.action: Replace the digitizer or the display unit that contains it

firstStep: Restart the device to rule out a frozen app
appliesWhen: the picture is fine but the device does not register touches in some or all areas
explanation: The digitizer is the touch layer on or in the display. When touch fails in an area after a restart and the picture is fine, the digitizer has failed and must be replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: each tap lands about a centimeter to the left of the finger
the tap offset is the same everywhere on the display
taps have landed off target since the display was replaced
a mouse points accurately while touch taps miss

answer.cause: a touchscreen that is out of calibration
answer.action: Calibrate the touchscreen in Tablet PC Settings

appliesWhen: touches register in every area but land at an offset from the finger
explanation: When every touch is shifted by the same amount, the touch input no longer lines up with the picture. In Windows, Control Panel > Tablet PC Settings > Calibrate lines them up again.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the pointer creeps slowly toward one side when no one touches anything
the laptop with the drifting pointer has a small red nub between the G and H keys
the creep starts after the user steers with that nub
an external mouse stays still when the user lets go of it, but the built-in pointer keeps creeping

answer.cause: a point stick that does not re-center
answer.action: Move the point stick back and forth to re-center it, then calibrate or disable it

appliesWhen: the pointer slowly moves by itself after the built-in stick is used
explanation: Cursor drift usually comes from a point stick that does not return to center after use. Moving it back and forth, calibrating it in Mouse properties, or rebooting fixes it; if not, disable or replace it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the active pen draws nothing on the tablet
finger touch works everywhere on the display, but the pen does not
the small light on the pen does not come on
the pen that draws nothing has not been charged since it was issued

answer.cause: a dead battery in the active stylus
answer.action: Charge or replace the stylus battery

appliesWhen: a powered pen does nothing while finger touch works
explanation: A powered stylus needs its own battery, so check the battery first when only the pen fails. After that, check the tip, the pairing, and any screen protector.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: pop-up ads appear even on the home screen
data use has tripled this month
the ads started after the user installed a game from a website instead of the store
the battery drains much faster than last week

answer.cause: a malicious app installed from outside the official store
answer.action: Remove the app, run a mobile antimalware scan, and update the operating system

appliesWhen: an app from an untrusted source shows ads and uses data and battery in the background
explanation: Malicious apps are the most common way that mobile devices get malware, and apps from outside the official stores are not vetted. Remove the app, scan the device, update the OS, and install apps only from official stores.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: every new app download stops with an error
the device that cannot install apps holds thousands of photos and videos
the storage page shows only 200 MB free
updates for the installed apps also fail

answer.cause: full device storage
answer.action: Delete unused apps, large files, and cached data to free space

firstStep: Check the free space on the storage settings page
appliesWhen: the device has almost no free space left for new apps
explanation: An app cannot install without enough free storage. Deleting unused apps, moving photos and videos off the device, and clearing caches frees the space.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the store says the app is not compatible with this device
the user of the device that cannot install the app has postponed every system update for over a year
the app will not install even though the device has 40 GB free
the same app installs on a coworker's device of the same model

answer.cause: an operating system version that is too old for the app
answer.action: Update the operating system and try the install again

appliesWhen: the app needs a newer OS version than the one installed
explanation: Many apps require a minimum OS version. A device that skips system updates cannot install them, even with plenty of space.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: apps open slowly and menus lag behind each tap
dozens of apps stay open in the app switcher of the slow device
the slow device has not been restarted in weeks
the device lags even though storage has plenty of free space

answer.cause: too many apps running in the background
answer.action: Close the background apps and restart the device

appliesWhen: the device is slow because many apps stay open and it is never restarted
explanation: Background apps use memory and processor time, and a device that runs for weeks without a restart slows down. Closing them and restarting frees resources; if it is still slow, update the OS and apps.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: the connection drops several times an hour at the far end of the building
the dropping connection stays stable in the room with the access point
the Wi-Fi icon shows only one bar at the user's desk
file copies slow to a crawl before each drop

answer.cause: a weak signal from too much distance to the access point
answer.action: Move the client closer to the access point or add another access point

firstStep: Check the signal strength at the user's location
appliesWhen: the client is far from the access point and the signal is weak
explanation: Distance is the most common cause of intermittent wireless connectivity, because the signal and the data rate fall fast as the client moves away. Moving closer or adding an access point restores a strong signal.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the Wi-Fi drops every day while the break room microwave runs
the laptop drops Wi-Fi even though it is close to the access point
the drops happen on a network that shares channel 6 with a dozen nearby networks
the Wi-Fi drops stop late at night

answer.cause: external interference on the 2.4 GHz band
answer.action: Move the clients to the 5 GHz band or change the wireless channel

appliesWhen: microwaves, motors, or neighbor networks disturb the signal even near the access point
explanation: Microwave ovens, motors, fluorescent lights, and nearby networks on the same channel disturb the 2.4 GHz band. A different channel or the 5 GHz band avoids the noise.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the whole office network is slow from 9 to 11 every morning
the slowdown matches the hours when many users stream video
the slow office network runs on old 100 Mbps switches
the network slowdown goes away in the evening

answer.cause: network congestion from too much traffic
answer.action: Upgrade the slow switches and limit bandwidth-heavy traffic

appliesWhen: many users load the network at the same time and the equipment is old
explanation: Slow speeds on a busy wired network usually mean the network carries more traffic than it can handle. Faster switches, VLANs, and less streaming reduce the load; the network is only as fast as its slowest part.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: only one wired PC copies files very slowly
the slow copies began after someone changed the network adapter's link settings by hand last month
the switch log shows many late collisions on that PC's port
the slow PC's patch cable passes a cable tester

answer.cause: a speed or duplex mismatch between the NIC and the switch port
answer.action: Set the NIC and the switch port to auto-negotiate speed and duplex

appliesWhen: the adapter and the switch port are set to different link speeds or duplex modes
explanation: When one end is forced to a fixed speed or half duplex and the other end is not, the link works but with many errors and low throughput. Letting both ends auto-negotiate fixes it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC cannot reach shares, printers, or the internet
ipconfig on the PC that cannot reach the network shows an address that starts with 169.254
several PCs on the same floor lost all network access at the same time this morning
the link light on the adapter is on, but the PC cannot reach any network resource

answer.cause: a DHCP server that does not answer
answer.action: Restore the DHCP server, then run ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew

firstStep: Run ipconfig /all to check the IP address
appliesWhen: the clients give themselves 169.254 addresses because no server hands out leases
explanation: A Windows client that gets no answer from a DHCP server assigns itself an APIPA address in 169.254.0.0/16 and can reach only other APIPA hosts. Fix the DHCP server, then renew the leases.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: websites will not open by name
ping 8.8.8.8 gets replies while websites fail to open
a share that fails by name opens when the user types the server's IP address
name lookups have failed since someone typed the IP settings by hand on this PC yesterday

answer.cause: a wrong DNS server address
answer.action: Correct the DNS server setting and flush the DNS cache

firstStep: Ping a remote host by IP address and then by name
appliesWhen: hosts answer by IP address but names do not resolve
explanation: If a host answers by IP address but not by name, name resolution is failing. Check the DNS server in ipconfig /all, correct it, and run ipconfig /flushdns.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC opens local file shares and the local printer but no internet sites
no internet sites load, even by IP address
ping to the router's address times out
other PCs on the same switch browse the internet normally, unlike this PC

answer.cause: a wrong default gateway setting
answer.action: Correct the default gateway in the IP settings

appliesWhen: local hosts work but nothing outside the local network answers
explanation: A client needs a default gateway to reach anything beyond its own subnet. Local access with no outside access on one PC points to a wrong gateway in its IP settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: a Windows pop-up warns about a conflict with another device on the network
the PC loses its connection every few minutes
the drops began after a coworker typed a fixed IP setting into his new PC last week
the connection still drops after the PC is restarted and its lease is renewed

answer.cause: a duplicate IP address on the network
answer.action: Give the static host an address outside the DHCP scope

appliesWhen: two hosts use the same IP address
explanation: Every host needs a unique IP address. A static address typed inside the DHCP scope gets handed out again by the server, so move the static host outside the scope or reserve its address.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: desk phone calls sound robotic and words drop out
the call problem is worst while the nightly backup copies files to the cloud
the choppy calls cross a router that still runs its factory settings
the calls break up although the phones are wired and data transfers finish normally

answer.cause: voice traffic competing with bulk data and no traffic priority
answer.action: Configure QoS on the router to give voice traffic priority

appliesWhen: voice calls break up only while large transfers share the link
explanation: VoIP needs a steady flow of small packets, and bulk transfers delay them. Quality of service lets the router send voice packets first, so calls stay clear when the link is busy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: video calls freeze for a second and then catch up
ping times to the gateway swing between 5 and 300 ms
the frozen calls run over a crowded wireless network
the same call is smooth from a desktop on an Ethernet cable

answer.cause: variable delay on a busy wireless link
answer.action: Connect the laptop with an Ethernet cable for calls

appliesWhen: delay changes from moment to moment on a wireless connection
explanation: Jitter is delay that changes from packet to packet, and it is more common on wireless links. A wired connection gives a steadier path; moving closer or using QoS also helps.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC's link light on the switch goes off and on over and over
a continuous ping shows bursts of lost replies
the cord of the PC that keeps losing its link is flattened where a chair rolls over it
only this one PC keeps losing its network link

answer.cause: a damaged patch cable
answer.action: Replace the patch cable and test the new one with a cable tester

firstStep: Check the port's link light on the switch
appliesWhen: the link goes up and down because the cord to the PC is crushed or worn
explanation: Port flapping is a link that keeps going up and down. A crushed patch cable is a common cause; replace and test it, then check the duplex and power-saving settings if it continues.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the workstation loses access to the servers in bursts several times a minute
the fiber uplink between the two switches goes down and up many times a minute
the switch error log shows the uplink problem on only one end
the workstation's own patch cord tests fine, but the drops to the servers continue

answer.cause: a faulty SFP transceiver
answer.action: Reseat the SFP module, then replace it with a known good one if the link still flaps

appliesWhen: a fiber link between switches flaps and its pluggable module is bad
explanation: SFPs are small hot-swappable transceivers used on gigabit and faster links. When an uplink flaps, reseat the SFPs and swap in known good ones.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: every web page and remote session lags on one PC
netstat -a on the lagging PC lists dozens of established connections
a file-sharing program runs in the background of the lagging PC
other PCs on the same network respond quickly while this one lags

answer.cause: too many open connections from background programs
answer.action: Close the unneeded programs and limit the data streams

appliesWhen: one host has many open connections that use up its bandwidth
explanation: Many open connections, such as torrent software, use the bandwidth and raise latency on that host. Closing the programs fixes it, and dozens of unknown connections may also be a sign of malware.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: every device loses the internet for a few minutes several times a day
local file shares and printers keep working during the internet drops
the modem's online light blinks during each drop
the router and switch show no errors during the internet drops

answer.cause: a problem on the internet provider's line
answer.action: Power cycle the modem and router, and contact the ISP if the drops continue

appliesWhen: every user loses only the internet while the local network keeps working
explanation: When all devices lose only internet access and the LAN keeps working, the fault is at the modem or beyond it. Restart the modem and router, then contact the ISP about outages or line noise.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the keyboard's A indicator light is lit while the password is rejected
the rejected password shows every letter as a capital when the user reveals it
the sign-in screen rejects the password but shows no lockout message

answer.cause: the Caps Lock key left on
answer.action: Turn off Caps Lock and type the password again

appliesWhen: the right password fails only because the letters are typed in the wrong case
explanation: The most common cause of an authentication failure is a wrongly typed password. Passwords are case-sensitive, so check the Caps Lock key before you look at the account or the server.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: sign-in has failed since the user mistyped the password several times this morning
the sign-in now fails even with the right password
a coworker signs in on the same PC while the user is refused
the message says the user cannot sign in at this time

answer.cause: a locked user account
answer.action: Unlock the account in Active Directory and reset the password if needed

appliesWhen: repeated wrong passwords have locked the account
explanation: Too many failed sign-ins lock the account, and then even the right password fails. An administrator unlocks it in Active Directory, and resets the password if the user has forgotten it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: the PC where the domain sign-in fails has a clock 25 minutes behind
domain sign-in fails on a PC that was off the network for a month
the user's account signs in fine on other PCs but not on this one
the error says the domain cannot verify the sign-in

answer.cause: a client clock out of sync with the domain controller
answer.action: Sync the PC's clock with the network time server

appliesWhen: the client's clock differs a lot from the server's time
explanation: Domain sign-in needs the client and server clocks to be close. Syncing the client with the NTP server fixes this type of authentication failure.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: no user in the branch office can sign in to the domain
only laptops that signed in before still open, with cached credentials
ping to the branch domain controller times out
users at the main office sign in normally while the branch cannot

answer.cause: an unreachable authentication server
answer.action: Restore the domain controller or the link to it

appliesWhen: the server that checks credentials is down or cannot be reached
explanation: If many users fail to authenticate at once, check that the authentication server, such as a domain controller or RADIUS server, is online and reachable. Escalate the problem if the server is outside your scope.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

clues: thin white streaks run from the top to the bottom of every page
the streaks are always in the same place
the printer with the white streaks is old and rarely serviced
the streaks appear although the toner level reads 70 percent

answer.cause: toner and debris stuck on the transfer corona wire
answer.action: Clean the corona wires with the corona brush

appliesWhen: white streaks run down every page of a laser printer
explanation: Foreign matter on the transfer corona wire keeps toner from reaching the paper at those spots, which leaves white streaks. Clean the corona wires with the small brush that comes with many laser printers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: a dark line runs down every page in the same place
the line stays after the paper path is cleaned
the printer with the dark line uses a cheap recycled toner cartridge
the line appeared after the cartridge was dropped

answer.cause: a scratched imaging drum
answer.action: Replace the toner cartridge or the imaging drum

appliesWhen: a dark line runs down every page because the drum surface is scratched
explanation: A scratch on the drum does not hold its charge, so toner sticks to it and prints a line down the page. Replace the cartridge, or the drum if the printer has a separate one.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: thin blank lines run through every line of text
the gaps in the text began after the printer sat unused for a month
the nozzle check page shows gaps in the black pattern
the blank lines appear although the ink levels read more than half full

answer.cause: dried ink clogging the printhead nozzles
answer.action: Run the printhead cleaning utility, and replace the cartridge if lines remain

appliesWhen: an inkjet sat unused and gaps run through the printed text
explanation: Ink dries in the tiny nozzles if an inkjet is not used every week or two, and each blocked nozzle leaves a blank line. The cleaning utility clears them; if not, a new cartridge with a new printhead does.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

clues: a thin white line runs through the middle of every line of characters
the line is at the same height in each character
a new ribbon did not remove the white line
the printer with the gap in its characters prints multipart invoices all day

answer.cause: a broken pin in the printhead
answer.action: Replace the printhead

appliesWhen: an impact printer leaves the same gap in every character after a new ribbon
explanation: A dot-matrix printhead forms each character with a row of pins. If one pin breaks or sticks, the same dot is missing in every character, so the printhead must be replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting
